title: Waqf in the longer ayat of Nuh: rule card and examples
subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
source: Written for quran/y8 lesson 40 (Pupil PDF worksheet: Waqf in the longer ayat of Nuh rule card and examples)
intro: Lesson 40. Read the rule and say every example aloud. Point to each word in your mushaf. Then answer the questions.

panels.title: Four kinds of stop
points: Tamm: complete, not linked to what follows
Kafi: complete in wording, linked in meaning
Hasan: sound, but the next words depend on it: restart earlier
Qabih: changes or breaks the meaning: avoid

arabic.text: وَإِنِّى كُلَّمَا دَعَوْتُهُمْ لِتَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ جَعَلُوٓا۟ أَصَٰبِعَهُمْ فِىٓ ءَاذَانِهِمْ وَٱسْتَغْشَوْا۟ ثِيَابَهُمْ وَأَصَرُّوا۟ وَٱسْتَكْبَرُوا۟ ٱسْتِكْبَارًۭا (٧)

keywords.def: stopping on a word, with a breath

questions.q: Recite 71:7 with two sound breath points and correct restarts.
questions.a: Breath after «لَهُمْ» and after «ثِيَابَهُمْ»; restart at «جَعَلُوٓا۟» or «وَأَصَرُّوا۟».

questions.q: Stop map (pupil PDF): mark signs and safe breath points in 71:1 to 12. Today's rota group recites Nuh 1 to 20.
questions.a: Signs in 71:4 marked; breath points in 71:1, 7 and 12 at clause ends.

questions.q: Extend: label the end of 71:9 tamm or kafi.
Stretch: why should 'emergency stops' be practised, not avoided?
questions.a: Long ayat need breath; practising sound stops protects the meaning.

questions.q: Stopping at «إِنَّ أَجَلَ ٱللَّهِ» and moving on is ...
options: a poor stop: the sentence is unfinished
questions.a: A) a poor stop: the sentence is unfinished. The sentence continues: 'when it comes, it will not be delayed'.

questions.q: Think again: 71:7 is a long ayah with no waqf sign. If you must breathe, how will you decide where?
questions.a: Stop where a complete idea ends and restart at the start of the next phrase.
